title: Design a Printable Café Menu
summary: A one-page A4 brunch menu for the fictional café Sunday Fern, delivered as an editable SVG and a 300 DPI PNG, then revised in the same conversation with new prices and a footer line.

source.title: How to Design a Printable Café Menu with AI

system:
You are a senior graphic designer who works in code. You plan a page before drawing it and you check your output before handing it over.

Technical constraints for print pieces:
- A4 portrait at 300 DPI is width="2480" height="3508" with viewBox="0 0 2480 3508". Use those exact attributes.
- The SVG must be self-contained: no external images, no web fonts, no <foreignObject>. Draw textures and illustrations with SVG shapes, paths and filters.
- Text stays as real <text> elements so the user can edit it later.
- The file is rendered with librsvg on macOS. Fonts installed there include Georgia, Didot, Baskerville, Hoefler Text, Big Caslon, Avenir Next, Gill Sans, Futura and Helvetica Neue. Name one of these first in every font-family list, then a generic family.
- Name deliverable files in kebab-case after the subject, for example acme-poster.svg. A PNG is exported automatically from every SVG you deliver, using the same base name, so deliver only the SVG.
review_prompt: Here is the PNG rendered from the SVG you just delivered, at half size. Check it the way you would before sending it to a print shop: overlapping or clipped text, prices on one clean right edge, nothing crowded at A4 size, illustrations legible, margins even. If anything needs fixing, deliver the corrected SVG under the same file name. If it is ready, say so in one or two sentences and deliver nothing.

turns.label: Brief
turns.prompt:
Design a vertical A4 menu for a small neighborhood brunch café called "Sunday Fern".
Three sections: Coffee, Brunch Plates, Fresh Juices — four items each. For every item include the name, a one-line description and a price in USD. Use realistic sample items and prices so I can swap them later.
Style: off-white textured paper, deep green ink, a clean serif for headings and a readable sans for body text, small hand-drawn botanical line illustrations, generous margins.
Make sure each price lines up clearly with its item and nothing is crowded at A4 print size.
Deliver a PNG for viewing and an editable SVG source file.

turns.label: Edit in the same task
turns.prompt: Update the SVG: change the three Coffee prices to $4.50, $5.25 and $5.75, make all prices slightly larger so they read well when printed, and add a footer line "Oat and almond milk available · Ask us about gluten-free options". Keep everything else. Save as "sunday-fern-menu-v2.svg" and export a matching PNG.

versions.name: v1
versions.change: First delivery from the brief: three sections of four items each, with sample USD prices. The self-check pass revised it once before hand-off.

versions.name: v2
versions.change: Coffee prices set to $4.50, $5.25 and $5.75; all prices slightly larger for print; new footer line "Oat and almond milk available · Ask us about gluten-free options". Everything else kept, and v1 left unchanged.
